records.title: compileOnly nullability annotations recognised by Kotlin

acceptanceCriteria.text: One nullability annotation library is declared `compileOnly` for every module of the root build and is absent from every module's `runtimeClasspath`. [D-026]

records.title: Dispatcher is the only RouteMatch-to-status mapping

records.requirement: The system shall map router lookup results and pre-checks to HTTP statuses only in the dispatcher, so the router stays engine-free and every adapter answers identically.
records.rationale: Durable rule of SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-3-3 (dispatcher, automatic responses, internal RestApp), moved to the SRS at SDS close.

records.title: Pre-checks run before any Request is built

acceptanceCriteria.text: For `OPTIONS *`, a raw path not starting with `/` and a raw path the path validator rejects, the dispatcher answers without constructing a `Request` and no handler, middleware or error handler is called.

records.requirement: The system shall run the pre-checks (`OPTIONS *`, raw path not starting with `/`, path validator) before any `Request` is built, so later middleware and `onError` may assume a non-null `Method` and a decoded path.
records.rationale: Durable rule of SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-3-3 (dispatcher, automatic responses, internal RestApp), moved to the SRS at SDS close.

records.title: A response commits status and headers at most once

acceptanceCriteria.text: For every response path (body writers, `end`, `stream`, automatic answers and failure answers), the exchange receives at most one call that starts the response (`commit`, `sendFile`, `upgrade` or `eventStream`).

records.requirement: The system shall commit a response's status and headers to the exchange at most once, because every adapter relies on a single commit call per exchange.
records.rationale: Durable rule of SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-3-5 (response writers and state machine), moved to the SRS at SDS close.

records.title: RestApp.create() looks up the bootstrap AppFactory through ServiceLoader

acceptanceCriteria.text: `RestApp.create()` is a `public static` method of the `RestApp` interface returning `RestApp`, and `RestApp` declares no other `create` overload. [D-110; residual: class-loader overload]

Through the internal lookup helper and a dedicated class loader that exposes exactly one fake provider at `META-INF/services/com.snoworca.naruserve.spi.AppFactory`, the helper returns the app the provider's `create()` returned. [D-226; wave decision: RestApp.create()] Decision: the lookup uses `ServiceLoader.load(AppFactory.class, loader)` where `RestApp.create()` passes `RestApp.class.getClassLoader()` and never the thread context class loader.

With a class loader that exposes no provider, the helper throws `IllegalStateException` whose message contains `com.snoworca.naruserve:NaruServe` and mentions `RestApp.builder()`; `RestApp.create()` itself throws that exception in the `NaruServe-api` test run, where no provider is on the class path. [D-227]
With a class loader that exposes two providers, the helper throws `IllegalStateException` whose message names both provider class names. [wave decision: RestApp.create()]

The fake providers live in the `NaruServe-api` `test` source set, not in its `testFixtures`, so no other module's tests see a provider, and `NaruServe-api` main has no compile-time reference to TinyHttpd or Gson. The provider classes are compiled in `src/test/java`, but their `META-INF/services/com.snoworca.naruserve.spi.AppFactory` file is not on the test class path: the test writes it into a temporary directory that only the dedicated class loader sees. [D-226; wave decision: RestApp.create()]

traceLinks.notes: the explicit entry point that a factory provider uses

records.requirement: The system shall provide the static interface method `RestApp.create()` that looks up the engine-free SPI `com.snoworca.naruserve.spi.AppFactory` (`RestApp create()`) with `ServiceLoader.load(AppFactory.class, RestApp.class.getClassLoader())` through a helper in `com.snoworca.naruserve.internal` and returns the app the single provider creates, throws an exception whose message names `com.snoworca.naruserve:NaruServe` when no provider is present and an exception naming every provider class when more than one is present.
records.rationale: Covers D-110 (declaration and lookup; the bootstrap factory and the end-to-end half are wave 5, `carried-into-wave-5.md`), the D-226 lookup and D-227 missing-module exception delivered by wave 4 (wave decision RestApp.create(), W2-001) and the residual on the class-loader overload (the helper lives in `internal`; `RestApp` gains no overload).

records.title: Per-app state isolation and the NEW-state guard

acceptanceCriteria.text: Two apps built in one JVM with different routes, middleware, loggers and `onStart` registrations each answer only their own routes, run only their own middleware, log only to their own logger and expose only their own services and attributes. [D-113]

A reflection scan finds no non-`final` static field and no static field of a mutable collection type in the classes of `com.snoworca.naruserve` and `com.snoworca.naruserve.internal` other than compile-time constants and `private static final` arrays that are never written after class initialisation (such as `MethodSet` `METHODS` and `DefaultResponse` `EMPTY`). [D-113]

In each of the states `STARTING` (called from an `onStart` callback), `RUNNING`, `STOPPING` (called from an `onStop` callback) and `TERMINATED`, each of `get`, `post`, `put`, `patch`, `delete`, `head`, `options`, `route(Method, ...)`, `route(MethodSet, ...)`, their route-middleware overloads, `use(mw)`, `use(prefix, mw)`, `accessLog`, `logger(l)`, `onStart`, `onStop`, `onError`, `routerPolicy` and the `get`/`use` methods of a `RouteBuilder` obtained in `NEW` throw `IllegalStateException` whose message names the method and the current state, and the refused call changes nothing. [D-114; wave-4 carried: NEW-state rule]

Every guarded method calls one internal guard method, so a test that lists by reflection all non-static `RestApp` methods returning `RestApp` (including `logger(Logger)`) and the registration methods of a `RouteBuilder` obtained from `route(String)` finds each one rejected in `RUNNING`, while `logger()`, `state()` and `route(String)` itself are not guarded. [D-114]

The after-freeze rejection of verified FR-HTTP-008 AC-5 still holds, because the one guard rejects when the state is not `NEW` or the route table is frozen (the harness and the FR-HTTP-008 tests freeze while the state is still `NEW`); FR-HTTP-008 AC-6 states the wave 3 situation that D-111 ends, and its wave 3 test is re-pointed to assert that `RestApp.builder()` and `RestApp.create()` are the only public static methods of `com.snoworca.naruserve` that return a `RestApp` or its builder. [D-114; D-111; wave-4 carried: NEW-state rule]

traceLinks.notes: replaces the after-freeze rejection with the NEW-state guard

records.requirement: The system shall keep each `RestApp`'s configuration, routes, middleware, service registry, application context and logger in that instance with no mutable static state shared between instances, and shall reject every registration and configuration method of `RestApp` and `RouteBuilder` with `IllegalStateException` when the app state is not `NEW`, through one internal state guard that later waves call for `ws`, `staticFiles`, `multipart` and `jsonCodec`.
records.rationale: Covers D-113, D-114 and the carried rule that the wave 3 after-freeze `IllegalStateException` becomes the `NEW`-state rule of D-114 and D-152.

records.title: Middleware scope and pipeline order in the dispatcher

acceptanceCriteria.text: With global middleware `g1`, `g2`, prefix middleware `p1` on `/api` registered before `g2` and `p2` on `/api`, and `app.route("/api/users").use(r1).use(r2).get(h)`, a `GET /api/users` records `g1, g2, p1, p2, r1, r2, h`, and `app.get("/b", r3, h2)` makes `GET /b` record `g1, g2, r3, h2`. [D-120; D-119; T35]

Prefix `/api` runs for `/api` and `/api/users` and not for `/apix` or `/ap`; prefix `/api/` behaves as `/api`, and prefix `/` runs for every path. [D-118; T35] Decision: a trailing `/` of a prefix is ignored and `/` covers every path.

With `RouterPolicy.builder().caseInsensitive(true)` the `/api` prefix middleware runs for `/API/users`, and with `mergeSlashes(true)` it runs for `//api//users`, so every path that reaches a route under the prefix runs the prefix middleware. [D-118] Decision: the prefix comparison uses the same case and slash normalisation that the router applies under the app's `RouterPolicy`.

Inside prefix middleware and the handler, `req.path()` still returns the full decoded path (for example `/api/users`, not `/users`). [D-118; D-137] Decision: NaruServe does not strip the mount prefix from `req.path()` and has no `baseUrl`.
A request that matches no route runs global and matching prefix middleware and then receives the `404` of the fallback point; route middleware of other routes does not run. [D-121; D-117]

A recording global middleware runs once each for a `405` (method mismatch), a `426` (WebSocket-only route without upgrade), an automatic `OPTIONS /r` `204`, a `501` for `TRACE /x` with `TRACE` disabled and a `501` for `CONNECT /`, before the automatic response is written. [D-117; wave decision: Pre-request rejections]

A global middleware does not run for the pre-request rejections (unrecognised method token `501`, raw path not starting with `/` `400`, `PathValidator` rejection `400`, `OPTIONS *` `204`) nor for the lifecycle-gate `503`s of FR-APP-009 and FR-APP-013. [wave decision: Pre-request rejections; wave decision: Lifecycle gate]
For a matched route all middleware and the handler run on the adapter thread that called the dispatcher, one after the other. [D-128]

traceLinks.notes: prefix comparison follows the path-form policies
tests run through the in-memory adapter

records.requirement: The system shall run, for every request for which a `Request` is built, all global middleware in registration order, then all prefix middleware whose prefix covers the path on a segment boundary in registration order, then, for a matched route, its route middleware in registration order and the handler, and, without a matched route, the dispatcher's fallback point, which answers the automatic `404`, `405`, `426`, `501` or `OPTIONS` response until wave 6 adds static mounts in front of it.
records.rationale: Covers D-117, D-118, D-120, D-121 and the wave decision on pre-request rejections (middleware runs for `404`, `405`, `426`, the automatic `OPTIONS` reply and the `501` of a disabled `TRACE` or `CONNECT`, including `CONNECT /`; the static-file and WebSocket-upgrade cases are asserted in waves 6 and 7). T35.

records.title: next.run() contract

acceptanceCriteria.text: A middleware that calls `next.run()` twice gets `IllegalStateException` from the second call, and the downstream middleware and handler ran once. [D-122; T35]

A middleware that calls `next.run()` after `res.send("x")` completed the response gets `IllegalStateException` and no downstream middleware runs; a `Next` kept and called after the request ended (from the test thread after the in-memory exchange finished) throws `IllegalStateException`. [D-123]
A middleware that records a marker after `next.run()` returns sees the handler's marker already recorded and `res.isCommitted()` true for a handler that called `res.send(...)`. [D-124]
A middleware that writes `res.status(401).send("no")` and returns without `next.run()` delivers `401` with body `no`, and the later middleware and the handler record no call. [D-125; T36]

Calling `next.error(e)` after `next.run()` in the same invocation, or `next.run()` after `next.error(e)`, throws `IllegalStateException`; `next.error(null)` throws `NullPointerException`. [D-122; D-116] Decision: `next.run()` and `next.error(e)` together count as the single continuation of one invocation.
`next.run()` runs the downstream chain on the calling thread, and no middleware or handler runs after the dispatcher returned to the adapter for a non-streaming response. [D-128]

records.requirement: The system shall let each middleware invocation continue the chain at most once through `next.run()` or `next.error(e)`, return from `next.run()` only after every downstream middleware and the handler returned, deliver the response of a middleware that responds without calling `next.run()` with no later middleware or handler run, and throw `IllegalStateException` for a second continuation within one invocation and for a continuation after the response completed or the request ended.
records.rationale: Covers D-122, D-123, D-124, D-125 and D-128 (synchronous execution). The unfinished-response case of D-126 is in the wave 4 successor of FR-HTTP-006. T35, T36.

records.title: Unified error path and onError chain

acceptanceCriteria.text: With one recording `onError`, a `RuntimeException` thrown by a middleware, a checked `IOException` thrown by a handler and `next.error(e)` from a middleware each reach the handler once with the same `Throwable` instance and the request's `Request` and `Response`. [D-127; D-129; T36]

An `HttpException(400)` thrown by a handler, an `HttpException(413)` and an `UnsupportedMediaTypeException` each reach `onError` with `status()` readable, and the malformed query `?x=%zz` raises an `HttpException` with status `400` that reaches `onError` after the middleware ran and before the handler. [D-129; D-130; wave-4 carried: malformed query]

With two `onError` handlers, the second runs only when the first returned with the response `NEW`, and receives the same error; when the first responded, the second records no call. [D-137] Decision: `onError` registrations form one chain in registration order that stops at the first handler that starts the response.
When every `onError` handler returned with the response `NEW`, or none is registered, the response is the standard error response of FR-APP-006 for the error. [D-132; D-137]

An `onError` handler that throws makes the framework log the thrown exception at `ERROR` through the app logger and answer the standard `500` error response if the response is still `NEW`; no later `onError` handler runs. [D-129; D-133]

When a handler throws while the response is `STREAMING`, `onError` is still called once, no error body is written, and after the error path the response is `ABORTED` with the in-memory exchange closed abnormally; when the response is `COMPLETED`, it stays `COMPLETED` with the sent bytes unchanged. [D-131; T37]

A recording `onError` records no call for the automatic `404`, `405`, `426`, `501` and `OPTIONS` responses and for the pre-request and lifecycle-gate rejections. [residual: onError scope; wave decision: Pre-request rejections]

An error that ends in a standard `500` response is logged once at `ERROR` with its `Throwable` through the app logger; an `HttpException` with a `4xx` status is not logged at `ERROR`. [D-129; D-133] Decision: only `500`s are logged at `ERROR`, with the stack trace kept in the server log.

The error path decides by the response state at the time the error arrives (`NEW` gives the error response, committed but not completed gives an abort, `COMPLETED` stays unchanged), the rule that the `res.json` serialisation case of D-136 relies on; that case itself is asserted in wave 5 once `res.json` exists. [D-136; D-131]

records.requirement: The system shall route an exception thrown by a middleware or handler and an error passed to `next.error(e)` to one error path that calls the registered `onError` handlers in registration order while the previous one left the response `NEW`, writes the standard error response of FR-APP-006 when the response is still `NEW` after them, and aborts instead of writing an error body when the response is already committed but not completed, while `onError` never receives the automatic `404`, `405`, `426`, `501` or `OPTIONS` responses.
records.rationale: Covers D-127, D-129, D-131, the D-137 decision on `onError` chaining, D-136 (asserted in wave 5 once `res.json` exists) and the residual on `onError` scope. Replaces the wave 3 interim failure handling (FR-HTTP-006, superseded in wave 4). T36, T37.

records.title: Standard error JSON body, status mapping and code values

acceptanceCriteria.text: A handler that throws `new RuntimeException("secret com.example.Foo")` is answered `500` with exactly `{"error":{"code":"INTERNAL_ERROR","message":"Internal Server Error","requestId":"<id>"}}`, `Content-Type: application/json; charset=UTF-8` and a matching `Content-Length`, and the body contains neither the exception message, nor `RuntimeException`, nor `at ` stack frames. [D-132; D-133]

The `code` values are `400` `BAD_REQUEST`, `404` `NOT_FOUND`, `405` `METHOD_NOT_ALLOWED`, `413` `PAYLOAD_TOO_LARGE`, `415` `UNSUPPORTED_MEDIA_TYPE`, `422` `UNPROCESSABLE_ENTITY`, `426` `UPGRADE_REQUIRED`, `500` `INTERNAL_ERROR`, `501` `NOT_IMPLEMENTED` and `503` `SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE`, and any other `HttpException` status uses `HTTP_<status>`. [D-134; D-137] Decision: these are the `code` values per status.

The `message` is the status reason phrase (for example `Not Found`), except for an `HttpException` created with a message, whose message is used; a `500` always uses `Internal Server Error`. [D-133; D-137] Decision: only an app-supplied `HttpException` message reaches the client.

Through the harness, a handler throwing `HttpException(400)`, `HttpException(422)`, `HttpException(413)` and `UnsupportedMediaTypeException` is answered `400`, `422`, `413` and `415` with the standard body, and any other exception `500`. [D-134; wave decision: 415]

The automatic `404`, `405` (with its `Allow` header), `426` (with `Upgrade: websocket` and `Connection: Upgrade`), `501`, the pre-request `400`s and `501` and the lifecycle-gate `503`s carry the standard body with their `code`; the `204` answers keep no body. [D-134; wave decision: 426 and 501; wave-4 carried: standard error body]
For a `HEAD` request the standard error response carries the headers and the `Content-Length` of the body it would have had and no body. [D-132; FR-HTTP-017]
The `requestId` of a standard error body equals the request id field of the access log line of FR-APP-015 for the same request, also for the pre-request rejections. [D-135]

The body is generated by the core without the app's `JsonCodec`, escapes `"`, `\` and control characters of the `message` per RFC 8259, and is identical with any codec. [D-132] Decision: the core writes the standard error JSON itself.
No API replaces the automatic `404`/`405` bodies in v1; an app answers custom `404` pages with a route of its own. [D-137] Decision: custom `404`/`405` bodies are not configurable in v1.

records.requirement: The system shall answer an error with no `onError` response, and the framework's own error statuses `400`, `404`, `405`, `426`, `501` and `503`, with the body `{"error":{"code":...,"message":...,"requestId":...}}`, `Content-Type: application/json; charset=UTF-8` and a `Content-Length`, using the status mapping of D-134 and the `code` values decided for #5, with no stack trace or exception class name and with `requestId` equal to the id the access log records for the request.
records.rationale: Covers D-132, D-133, D-134, D-135, the D-137 decisions on `code` values per status and on custom `404`/`405` bodies, the wave decisions on `415`, on `426` and `501` (automatic responses with the standard body) and on overload `503` (a full TinyHttpd queue is a transport-level `503`, D-400, not standard JSON), and the carried line that wave 4 gives the error statuses the standard error body.

records.title: Service registration, frozen registry and the single application context

acceptanceCriteria.text: A `UserService` registered in `onStart` is returned with identity by `req.service(UserService.class)` and `req.application().get(UserService.class)` in an HTTP handler; the WebSocket and SSE cases of D-142 are asserted in wave 7. [D-142; T41; wave decision: Services for long connections]

`ctx.register` and `ctx.registerExternal` called from `onStop`, and `req.application().register(...)` called from a handler in `RUNNING`, throw `IllegalStateException`, and the registry is unchanged. [D-139; D-141; T42]

A second `ctx.register(UserService.class, other)` in `onStart` throws `IllegalStateException` naming the key, so `listen()` fails with it, and `getOrNull(UserService.class)` read from a failing-start close hook still returns the first instance. [D-140; T42] Decision: the configuration error is `IllegalStateException`.

In `RUNNING` sixteen threads calling `req.service(UserService.class)` concurrently all receive the registered instance, and the registry seen in `RUNNING` is an unmodifiable snapshot taken before the state became `RUNNING`. [D-141]
Two `onStart` callbacks run in registration order, each exactly once for one successful `listen()`, and neither runs again on `shutdown`. [D-143; D-154; T41]

`ctx.attribute` set in `onStart` is read by handlers in `RUNNING` and by `onStop` in `STOPPING`, and eight threads writing and reading distinct keys concurrently during `RUNNING` lose no write, and `onStop` writes `ctx.attribute("k2", v)` and reads it back. [D-144]
`ctx.logger()` in `onStart` and `onStop` returns the same instance as `app.logger()`, also after `app.logger(l)` replaced it before `listen`. [D-145]
The `ctx` passed to `onStart`, the `ctx` passed to `onStop` and `req.application()` in every request are the same instance. [D-146]

records.requirement: The system shall accept `ctx.register` and `ctx.registerExternal` only while the app is `STARTING` and the `onStart` callbacks run, reject a second registration of the same `Class` key without replacing the first instance, freeze the registry into an immutable snapshot before `RUNNING`, run each `onStart` callback exactly once per successful `listen()`, keep exactly one `ApplicationContext` per app, which `onStart`, `onStop` and `req.application()` all receive, and return from `req.service(T)` the instance `req.application().get(T)` returns.
records.rationale: Covers D-139, D-140, D-141, D-142 (HTTP handlers; the WebSocket and SSE cases are wave 7, `carried-into-wave-7.md`), D-143, D-144, D-145 and D-146. T41, T42.

records.title: Owned and registered resources close once in reverse order

acceptanceCriteria.text: `ctx.own(db)`, then `ctx.register(UserService.class, users)` (an `AutoCloseable`) close as `users`, then `db` on shutdown. [D-147; D-149; T45]
One object registered under an interface key and under its implementation key and also owned is closed exactly once, at the position of its first `own` or `register` call. [D-148; T45]

When the second of three resources throws from `close()`, the first and third are still closed; on shutdown the failure is logged at `ERROR` through the app logger, and on start failure it is added as a suppressed exception to the exception `listen()` throws. [D-150; D-158] Decision: close failures are logged on shutdown and attached as suppressed on start failure.

An object registered only with `registerExternal` is not closed on shutdown or start failure, while `get` returns it like any service; an object passed to both `registerExternal` and `own` is closed once. [D-151]
A non-`AutoCloseable` service is registered and returned normally and nothing is closed for it. [D-149]

records.requirement: The system shall close every object passed to `ctx.own` and every `AutoCloseable` passed to `ctx.register` on shutdown and on start failure, exactly once per object compared by identity, in reverse order of each object's first `own` or `register` call, continuing after a failing `close()`, and shall never close an object registered only through `registerExternal`.
records.rationale: Covers D-147, D-148, D-149, D-150 and the D-151 decision (`registerExternal`). T43, T45.

records.title: listen() startup sequence and the start gate

acceptanceCriteria.text: Two threads calling `listen(0)` at the same time on a `NEW` app: exactly one proceeds and the other gets `IllegalStateException`; a second `listen` after a successful one throws `IllegalStateException`. [D-153]

A recording test adapter and callbacks observe the order: state `STARTING`, `onStart` callbacks in registration order, route-table freeze, one `bind` call, state `RUNNING`, `listen` returns. [D-154; wave-4 carried: listen runs the route-table freeze]
A duplicate route of D-044 makes `listen()` throw the freeze's `RoutingConfigException` after the `onStart` callbacks ran and before any `bind` call. [D-154; D-157]
`listen()` returns only after `bind` returned, and the returned `ServerHandle` reports the bound port. [D-155]

With a test adapter whose `bind` dispatches a request from another thread before returning, the request's middleware and handler run only after `app.state()` is `RUNNING` (asserted inside the handler), and the request is answered normally. [D-156; D-428]

With a test adapter whose `bind` dispatches a request from another thread and then throws `IOException`, the held request is answered `503` with `Connection: close` and the standard error body, and no middleware, handler or `onError` runs for it. [D-428; wave decision: Lifecycle gate; wave decision: STARTING]

The test-fixtures harness `TestApp` builds its app with `RestApp.builder().httpAdapter(inMemoryAdapter).jsonCodec(stubCodec)` (a stub `JsonCodec` in the test fixtures) and its `start()` calls `listen(0)`, which runs the route-table freeze once, so a `RoutingConfigException` of the freeze still reaches the test caller unwrapped and every wave 3 test through `TestApp` that cites a requirement wave 4 does not supersede keeps passing unchanged, while the tests citing FR-HTTP-002, FR-HTTP-003, FR-HTTP-005, FR-HTTP-006 or FR-HTTP-010 are re-pointed to FR-HTTP-021..FR-HTTP-025 and assert the standard error body (a requirement change, not a weakened test); verified FR-HTTP-001 AC-3 (the harness builds the internal implementation and runs the freeze once) still holds. [wave-4 carried: listen runs the route-table freeze; D-154]

The start gate and the lifecycle gate belong to the exchange handler that `listen()` passes to the adapter; the wave 3 `Dispatcher(Router)` constructor and `DefaultRestApp.dispatcher()` that unit tests bind without `listen()` stay ungated, so those verified wave 3 unit tests keep dispatching. [D-428; D-156] Decision: the gates wrap the dispatcher instead of living inside it.

records.requirement: The system shall move the app from `NEW` to `STARTING` atomically in `listen()`, rejecting a second or concurrent `listen()`, then run the `onStart` callbacks in registration order, freeze and validate the router, registry and options with the wave 3 route-table freeze, bind and start accepting through the adapter in one call, enter `RUNNING` and return a `ServerHandle`, while the dispatcher holds every request that reaches it before `RUNNING` on a start gate, releases it into the pipeline once `RUNNING` is set and answers it `503` with `Connection: close` when the start fails or a pending stop ends it.
records.rationale: Covers D-153, D-154, D-155, D-156, D-428, the wave decisions on `STARTING` and on the lifecycle gate (gate answers skip middleware and `onError` but get an access-log line and the standard error body) and the carried line that `listen()` runs the same route-table freeze as the wave 3 harness.

records.title: Start failure leaves no socket and closes resources

acceptanceCriteria.text: An `onStart` that throws `IllegalArgumentException` makes `listen()` throw that same instance, and the recording test adapter saw no `bind` call. [D-157; D-159; T43]
An `onStart` that throws `IOException` makes `listen()` throw `AppStartException` whose cause is that `IOException`. [D-159]

A bind failure (`bind` throws `IOException`) makes `listen()` throw `AppStartException` with that cause, after which the core called the adapter's `stop` and `release`, which the in-memory adapter and the recording test adapter accept without a bound socket, so the adapter holds no socket. [D-157; D-159]

Resources owned and registered before an `onStart` failure are closed in reverse order before `listen()` throws, and a resource's `close()` reads `app.state()` as `FAILED`; after `listen()` threw, `app.state()` is `TERMINATED`. [D-158; D-159; T43]
No `onStop` callback runs for any start failure. [D-160]

With a rotating file logger of FR-APP-017 as the app logger, no writer thread of it remains after a failed `listen()` (a test in `NaruServe-filelog`), and a console app logger that is also owned is closed once. [residual: Logger close on every path into TERMINATED; D-148; I-015]

traceLinks.notes: rotating file logger case of AC-6

records.requirement: The system shall, when an `onStart` callback, the freeze validation or the adapter bind fails, leave no listening socket open, never run `onStop`, move the state to `FAILED`, close the already owned and registered resources in reverse order, flush and close the app logger in the final log-writer step, move to `TERMINATED` and throw the cause from `listen()`, an unchecked cause as is and a checked cause wrapped in `AppStartException`.
records.rationale: Covers D-157, D-158, D-159, D-160 and the residual on closing the logger on every path into `TERMINATED` (failed start). T43.

records.title: Shutdown sequence, deadline and shutdown participants

acceptanceCriteria.text: A recording test adapter, participants in all three phases, an `onStop` callback, an owned resource and a `Flushable`/`AutoCloseable` app logger record the order: before-wait participants, `adapter.stop`, force-close participants, `onStop`, after-`onStop` participants, owned resource `close`, logger `flush` and `close`, `adapter.release`, then `app.state()` is `TERMINATED`. [D-162; D-401; T46]

The timeout passed to `adapter.stop` is the time left until the one deadline computed when `shutdown` began, so a before-wait participant that sleeps 200 ms of a 1 s timeout leaves at most 800 ms for the adapter stop. [D-162; wave-4 carried: exchange lifetime]
The internal participant registry adds participants to a phase in order and runs them in that order; a participant that throws is logged at `ERROR` and the sequence continues. [D-401]
`onStop` reads every service registered in `onStart` through `ctx.get`, before any owned resource is closed. [D-163; T45]
Two threads calling `shutdown` on a `RUNNING` app: one runs the sequence; the other and any later call return without running any step again, and `onStop` ran once. [D-161; T46]
A request in flight when `shutdown` begins completes normally while the adapter stop waits within the deadline. [D-162]
An app logger that is also owned is skipped at its owned position and closed once at the log-writer step; closing the console logger leaves `System.out` open. [wave decision: Logger shutdown; D-148]
An `onStop` callback that throws is logged at `ERROR`, the remaining `onStop` callbacks run and the sequence continues to `TERMINATED`. [D-162] Decision: `onStop` failures do not stop shutdown.

traceLinks.notes: exchange outlives handle until finish or abort; force-close at the deadline

records.requirement: The system shall move a `RUNNING` app to `STOPPING` atomically on the first `shutdown(timeout, unit)` call, compute one deadline from the timeout and run in order the before-wait participants, the adapter stop up to the deadline, the force-close participants, the `onStop` callbacks once while services are still registered, the after-`onStop` participants, closing owned and registered resources in reverse order, flushing and closing the app logger, the adapter release and the move to `TERMINATED`, through an internal shutdown participant registry with these three fixed phases.
records.rationale: Covers D-161, D-162, D-163, D-401, the wave decision on logger shutdown and the carried line that the adapter may force-close only at the stop deadline. Wave 6 adds temporary-file cleanup (D-255) as an after-`onStop` participant and wave 7 adds WebSocket (D-435) and SSE (D-436) closing as before-wait participants. T45, T46.

records.title: shutdown in NEW, STARTING, FAILED and TERMINATED, and listen after termination

acceptanceCriteria.text: `shutdown` on a `NEW` app sets `TERMINATED`, runs no `onStart` or `onStop` callback, never calls the adapter's `bind`, and closes a `Flushable`/`AutoCloseable` app logger once. [D-164; residual: Logger close on every path into TERMINATED]

With `onStart` blocked on a latch inside `listen()` on thread A, `shutdown(5, SECONDS)` on thread B, then the latch released: `onStart` finishes, no `bind` happens, `listen()` throws `AppStartException`, no `onStop` runs, owned resources close in reverse order and observe `FAILED`, `app.state()` ends `TERMINATED`, and `shutdown` returns after `listen()` ended, and a `Flushable`/`AutoCloseable` app logger is flushed and closed once after the resources closed and before `TERMINATED`. [D-426; T46; residual: Logger close on every path into TERMINATED] Decision: a start ended by a pending stop throws `AppStartException` with a message saying shutdown was requested while starting. Decision: with a pending stop recorded during `onStart` callback k, the callbacks registered after k do not run; the latch test registers a second callback and asserts it never ran.

When the pending stop is recorded during `bind`, the socket bound by it is released (`stop` and `release` called) and `RUNNING` is never set, and a request that the test adapter dispatched during that `bind` is answered `503` with `Connection: close` and the standard error body with no middleware, handler or `onError` run. [D-426; D-428]

With `onStart` blocked on a latch, `shutdown(100, MILLISECONDS)` returns normally without an exception before the latch is released, `app.state()` is then `STARTING` or `FAILED`, and once the latch is released `listen()` still passes through `FAILED` to `TERMINATED` and throws `AppStartException`. [D-438; T46]

A resource `close()` running during a failing `listen()` (state `FAILED`) starts thread B, which calls `shutdown(5, SECONDS)`, and then blocks 100 ms; B's `shutdown` returns after the state became `TERMINATED` and within its timeout; `shutdown` on a `TERMINATED` app returns at once with no callback or close run. [D-427]
`listen(0)` on a `TERMINATED` app throws `IllegalStateException`. [D-165; T46]

records.requirement: The system shall move a `NEW` app to `TERMINATED` on `shutdown` without running `onStart` or `onStop`, record a pending stop for a `shutdown` during `STARTING` and wait up to its timeout for `listen()` to end, which then finishes the step in progress, closes any bound socket, never enters `RUNNING`, never runs `onStop`, closes resources in reverse order and then flushes and closes the app logger, passes through `FAILED` to `TERMINATED` and throws `AppStartException`, return normally when that timeout passes first, wait up to the timeout for a `FAILED` app to reach `TERMINATED`, return at once for a `TERMINATED` app, and reject `listen()` on a `TERMINATED` app.
records.rationale: Covers D-164, D-165, D-426, D-427, D-438 and the residual on closing the logger on every path into `TERMINATED` (stop while starting, shutdown before start). T46.

records.title: Requests reaching the dispatcher during STOPPING get 503 with Connection: close

acceptanceCriteria.text: A request sent through the in-memory adapter from a before-wait shutdown participant (after `STOPPING` began, before the adapter stop) is answered `503` with `Connection: close` and `{"error":{"code":"SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE",...}}`. [D-166; D-134; wave decision: Keep-alive at shutdown]

For that request a recording global middleware, the route handler and a recording `onError` record no call, and the access log records exactly one line with status `503`. [wave decision: Lifecycle gate; D-173]
A request that was in flight when `STOPPING` began is not answered `503` and completes with its handler's response. [D-166; D-162]

The lifecycle gate runs before the pre-request checks, so during `STOPPING` an `OPTIONS *`, an unrecognised method token and a raw path not starting with `/` are each answered `503` with `Connection: close` and the standard error body, and in `STARTING` they are held on the start gate like any request. [wave decision: Lifecycle gate; D-428] Decision: the lifecycle gate is the first check of the exchange handler that `listen()` passes to the adapter, which wraps the dispatcher (FR-APP-009 AC-8).

records.requirement: The system shall answer every request that reaches the dispatcher after `STOPPING` began with `503`, `Connection: close` and the standard error body, at the lifecycle gate before the pipeline, so no middleware, handler or `onError` runs for it while it still gets one access-log line.
records.rationale: Covers D-166 for the in-memory adapter and the wave decisions on keep-alive at shutdown and on the lifecycle gate. The TinyHttpd keep-alive socket case and T44 are wave 5 (`carried-into-wave-5.md`). D-134 maps a request arriving during `STOPPING` to `503`.

records.title: Logger failures never interrupt requests or the server

acceptanceCriteria.text: With an app logger whose six methods all throw `RuntimeException`, a request to a route is answered with its handler's response, a handler exception is still answered with the standard `500` body, and an unfinished response is still finished. [D-171]
With that logger, `listen(0)` returns `RUNNING`, and `shutdown` reaches `TERMINATED` even when the logger's `flush` and `close` also throw. [D-171]
No exception thrown by the logger reaches the adapter's `ExchangeHandler` caller or the thread that called `listen` or `shutdown`. [D-171]

records.requirement: The system shall catch every `RuntimeException` thrown by the app logger or a log writer when the framework logs (access log, developer warnings, error logging, lifecycle logging, flush and close), so request processing, `listen()` and `shutdown()` complete as they would with a working logger.
records.rationale: Covers D-171.

records.title: One access log line per HTTP request

acceptanceCriteria.text: With the defaults, `GET /users/7` answered `200` with a 5-byte body produces exactly one `info` line matching `GET /users/7 200 \d+ms in=0 out=5 rid=[0-9a-f]{16}`. [D-173; D-181; T38] Decision: this is the line format, and the request id is 16 lowercase hex characters generated per request.
With `includeDuration(false)`, `includeBytes(false)` and `includeRequestId(false)` the line is `GET /users/7 200`, and with `level(LogLevel.DEBUG)` it is written through `debug`. [D-172; D-173]

A response aborted after commit (handler throws while `STREAMING`) produces one line with its committed status followed by ` aborted`; a `404`, a `405`, a handler `500`, each pre-request rejection (`501` unknown token, `400` raw path, `400` validator, `204` `OPTIONS *`) and each lifecycle-gate `503` produce exactly one line. [D-173; wave decision: Pre-request rejections; wave decision: Lifecycle gate]
For a streaming response the line is written once after the stream copy finished, with `out` equal to the bytes copied; for a `HEAD` response `out` is `0`. [D-173; D-177]

`in` counts the request body bytes the core read from the adapter's body stream (not the declared `Content-Length`): a dispatcher test whose handler reads 4 bytes of a 10-byte body through the internal `BodyState` stream logs `in=4`, and a handler that never reads gives `in=0`. [D-177]

After `exclude("/health")`, `GET /health` produces no line while `GET /health/x` and `GET /healthz` do; with `enabled(false)` no request produces a line. [D-174; D-172] Decision: `exclude` matches the raw path without the query exactly.
The `rid` value of the line equals the `requestId` of the standard error body of the same request. [D-135]

traceLinks.notes: requestId shared with the error body

records.requirement: The system shall write through the app logger at the configured level exactly one access log line per HTTP request that reaches the dispatcher, when the response completes or is aborted, in the format `<method> <path> <status>[ aborted][ <duration>ms][ in=<bytesIn> out=<bytesOut>][ rid=<requestId>]`, where `path` is the raw path without the query, the optional parts follow the options of IR-APP-007, the byte fields count body bytes actually read from and written to the connection, and requests to an excluded path produce no line.
records.rationale: Covers D-173 (HTTP part of T38), D-174, D-177, D-135 and the D-181 decision on the line format, plus the wave decisions that the three pre-request rejections and the two lifecycle-gate `503`s also get exactly one line; only TinyHttpd's transport-level rejections (D-400) have none.

records.title: Logcat logger through reflection on android.util.Log

acceptanceCriteria.text: A JVM test in `NaruServe-logcat` with a test-scope fake `android.util.Log` that records calls shows `new LogcatLogger()` calling `v`, `d`, `i`, `w`, `e(tag, msg)` and `e(tag, msg, t)` with tag `NaruServe` for the six methods. [D-403] Decision: the default tag is `NaruServe`.
`new LogcatLogger("MyApp")` uses tag `MyApp`, and `new LogcatLogger(null)` throws `NullPointerException`. [D-403]

Without `android.util.Log` on the class path, the `LogcatLogger` constructor throws `IllegalStateException` naming `android.util.Log`; an exception thrown by a reflective call is caught and not rethrown. The case without `android.util.Log` loads `LogcatLogger` through a dedicated class loader that sees the `NaruServe-logcat` and `NaruServe-api` main classes but not the test classes. [D-403; D-171]

The `NaruServe-logcat` main classes reference no `android.*` type in their bytecode; `android.util.Log` appears only as a string for reflection, and the fake class lives only in the test source set. [D-403; D-178]

records.requirement: The system shall provide in `NaruServe-logcat` the public `com.snoworca.naruserve.logcat.LogcatLogger implements Logger` that maps `trace`, `debug`, `info`, `warn`, `error(String)` and `error(String, Throwable)` to `android.util.Log.v`, `d`, `i`, `w`, `e(String, String)` and `e(String, String, Throwable)` looked up by reflection, with the default tag `NaruServe` and a constructor taking a tag.
records.rationale: Covers D-403 and the D-181 decision on the Logcat tag. The module builds without an Android SDK (wave 1). `RestApp.create()` choosing it on Android is D-402, wave 5.

records.title: Rotating file logger with a bounded queue

acceptanceCriteria.text: `RotatingFileLogger.builder().build()` uses directory `./logs`, `maxFileBytes` `5242880`, `maxFiles` `5`, `queueCapacity` `1024` and level `INFO`; `maxFileBytes`, `maxFiles` or `queueCapacity` below `1` throw `IllegalArgumentException`. [D-180; I-012] Decision: the queue capacity defaults to 1024 records and no value may be unlimited.

Records are written to `naruserve.log` in the console line format of IR-APP-006; when the next record would exceed `maxFileBytes` the files rotate to `naruserve.log.1` up to `naruserve.log.<maxFiles-1>`, dropping the oldest, so a test with `maxFileBytes(200)` and `maxFiles(3)` ends with at most three files. [D-180] Decision: the file names are `naruserve.log` and `naruserve.log.<n>`.
With the writer blocked on a latch inside the test output stream and `queueCapacity(2)`, the third and later records are dropped without blocking the caller and `droppedCount()` counts them. [D-180]
With a directory that cannot be created, logging calls return normally and `droppedCount()` grows; no exception reaches the caller. [wave decision: File logger directory; D-171]

`flush()` returns after every record queued before the call is written; `close()` writes the queued records, stops the writer thread so no thread of the logger remains, and later logging calls are dropped and counted. [wave decision: Logger shutdown; I-015]
The module's main classes reference no SLF4J or `android.*` type and pass the API 21 animal-sniffer check. [D-179; C-02]

The tests of this requirement and the failed-`listen()` writer-thread check of FR-APP-010 AC-6 live in the `NaruServe-filelog` test source set, which declares `testImplementation testFixtures(project(':NaruServe-api'))`; tests block the writer through a package-private constructor that takes the factory of the file output stream. [D-180; I-015]

records.requirement: The system shall provide in `NaruServe-filelog` the public `com.snoworca.naruserve.filelog.RotatingFileLogger implements Logger, Flushable, AutoCloseable`, built with `RotatingFileLogger.builder()` (`directory`, `maxFileBytes`, `maxFiles`, `queueCapacity`, `level`, `build()`), that hands records to one writer thread through a bounded queue with a drop counter, rotates files, defaults to directory `./logs`, 5 MiB per file and 5 files, and stops its writer thread in `close()`.
records.rationale: Covers D-180, D-179 (module placement), the wave decisions on logger shutdown (implements `AutoCloseable`, no writer thread outlives shutdown, I-015) and on the file logger directory (Android apps pass a writable directory; an unwritable one drops and counts records without stopping the HTTP service).

records.title: SLF4J logger adapter

acceptanceCriteria.text: A test with a recording `org.slf4j.Logger` shows each of the six methods forwarded once to the matching SLF4J method with the same message and throwable. [D-179]

`new Slf4jLogger()` delegates to the SLF4J logger named `NaruServe`, checked through a hand-written test-scope `org.slf4j.impl.StaticLoggerBinder` whose `ILoggerFactory` records the requested names (slf4j-api 1.7.36 binding mechanism), which leaves the runtime dependencies binding-free, and `new Slf4jLogger(null)` throws `NullPointerException`. [D-179]
`Slf4jLogger` lives only in `NaruServe-slf4j`, and `NaruServe-api` contains no class of the package `com.snoworca.naruserve.slf4j`. [D-179; T40]
The recording `org.slf4j.Logger` is a hand-written implementation in the `NaruServe-slf4j` test source set, so the module adds no SLF4J binding to its runtime dependencies. [D-179]

records.requirement: The system shall provide in the JVM-only module `NaruServe-slf4j` the public `com.snoworca.naruserve.slf4j.Slf4jLogger implements Logger` that forwards the six methods to `org.slf4j.Logger` `trace`, `debug`, `info`, `warn`, `error(String)` and `error(String, Throwable)`, with a constructor taking an `org.slf4j.Logger` and a no-argument constructor using `LoggerFactory.getLogger("NaruServe")`.
records.rationale: Covers D-179 (the SLF4J adapter in its optional module, T40).

records.title: In-memory HttpAdapter and test harness in the test fixtures

acceptanceCriteria.text: The in-memory adapter is a class under `NaruServe-api/src/testFixtures/java` implementing `HttpAdapter`, it is packaged in the `NaruServe-api` test-fixtures jar (CON-BUILD-006 AC-8), and `NaruServe-api`'s own tests use it. [D-108]

A request sent through the in-memory adapter passes through the same dispatcher, router, `Request` and `Response` code as an adapter in production, opens no socket, and returns the status, headers and body bytes the core wrote. [D-108]

The harness builds the internal `RestApp` implementation over the in-memory adapter, runs the route-table freeze once and then sends requests, and a registration error raised by the freeze reaches the test caller as the thrown exception. [wave decision: Working app in wave 3; D-397] Decision: the harness `start()` rethrows the freeze's `RoutingConfigException` itself, unwrapped. [SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-3-2 SDS-AC-8]

The in-memory adapter passes the request-target path and query string to the core undecoded, so `GET /a%20b?q=%20` reaches `req.rawPath()` = `/a%20b` and the raw query `q=%20` (`req.query("q")` = ` `). [D-399; wave decision: Adapter halves]

The in-memory adapter answers an authority-form `CONNECT host:443` request itself with `501` without calling the dispatcher, mirroring TinyHttpd. [wave-3 carried: CONNECT authority-form; I-021] Decision: any `CONNECT` whose target does not start with `/` gets `501` with `Content-Length: 0`, and the `ExchangeHandler` is not called. [SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-3-2 SDS-AC-9]

The in-memory adapter rewrites an absolute-form target such as `http://example.com/a?x=1` to raw path `/a` and raw query `x=1` before dispatch, mirroring TinyHttpd. [wave-3 carried: absolute-form target; I-021] Decision: of an absolute-form `scheme://authority/path?query` target only the path (or `/` when the path is empty) and the query are kept. [SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-3-2 SDS-AC-10]
The in-memory adapter passes an asterisk-form `OPTIONS *` target to the core as raw path `*`, as TinyHttpd does. [D-442; I-021; loop D: V1-006/V2-004]

records.title: Dispatcher pipeline and pre-request checks before route lookup

acceptanceCriteria.text: Through the harness, a `GET /users/7` request with `app.get("/users/:id", h)` registered reaches `h` once with a `Request` and a `Response`, and the status, headers and body `h` wrote come back through the in-memory adapter. [D-394; D-397]

With a recording handler registered through `app.route(Method.any(), "/", h)` and `app.route(Method.any(), "/:x", h)`, `OPTIONS *` is answered `204` before path validation (so `*` is not rejected with `400`), and a validator rejection happens before the router lookup: `GET /%2e%2e` and `GET /a%2Fb` (both rejected by the `PathValidator`) are answered `400`, no lookup exception escapes, and `h` registered on the matching pattern `/:x` records no call. [wave decision: Order before lookup; D-442; D-052] Decision: the dispatcher checks in this order: `OPTIONS` with raw path `*` gives `204`, any raw path not starting with `/` gives `400`, a `PathValidator` rejection gives `400`, then the router lookup runs. [SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-3-3 SDS-AC-1]

A raw path that the wave 2 `PathValidator` rejects is answered `400` with `Content-Length: 0` and an empty body without a router lookup, and the validator sees the raw form with a single decoding: `/%2e%2e` and `/a%2Fb` are answered `400`, while `/%252e%252e` reaches a `/:x` route with `req.param("x")` = `%2e%2e`. [wave-3 carried: path validator before lookup; D-052; wave decision: Automatic response bodies]

An unrecognised method token is answered `501`, a raw path not starting with `/` `400`, a validator rejection `400` and `OPTIONS *` `204`, each before a `Request` is built, so no handler sees them; a recording handler registered through `app.route(Method.any(), "/", h)` and `app.route(Method.any(), "/:x", h)` records that it was never called. [wave-3 residual: pre-request rejections; D-422]
In every handler call `req.method()` returns a non-null `Method` and `req.path()` a non-null decoded path. [wave-3 residual: pre-request rejections]

records.title: Automatic responses for router lookup results

acceptanceCriteria.text: Through the harness, a request whose path matches no route is answered `404` with `Content-Length: 0` and, in wave 3 (until wave 4 adds the standard error body), an empty body. [D-395; wave decision: Automatic response bodies]

With only `POST /p` registered, `GET /p` is answered `405` with `Allow` listing `POST, OPTIONS`, and with `GET /r` registered `DELETE /r` is answered `405` with `Allow` including the automatic `HEAD` and `OPTIONS`, both with `Content-Length: 0` in wave 3. [D-395; T02] Decision: the `Allow` value joins the allowed methods (or `Method.any()` for `OPTIONS *`) with `, ` in `MethodSet` iteration (`Method` declaration) order. [SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-3-3 SDS-AC-3]

With `GET /r` and `POST /r` registered and no `OPTIONS` route, `OPTIONS /r` is answered `204` with `Allow` = `GET, HEAD, POST, OPTIONS`, no body and no `Content-Length` header. [D-395; T05; wave decision: Automatic response bodies]
A request with an unsupported method token is answered `501` with `Content-Length: 0` and, in wave 3, an empty body. [D-395]

With a WebSocket-only route registered through the internal hook of FR-HTTP-008 AC-7, a plain `GET` to that path is answered `426` with headers `Upgrade: websocket` and `Connection: Upgrade` and, in wave 3, `Content-Length: 0`, asserted through the in-memory adapter. [D-395; T06; wave decision: 426 over TinyHttpd] Decision: the upgrade flag passed to the lookup is `Router.isWebSocketUpgrade(token, Connection, Upgrade)` with each header's values joined by `, `. [SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-3-3 SDS-AC-4]

With the same WebSocket-only hook route, a `GET` carrying `Upgrade: websocket` and `Connection: Upgrade` (for which the router returns a `MATCHED` result with route kind `WEBSOCKET`) is answered in wave 3 with the same `426`, both headers and `Content-Length: 0`, and no handshake is attempted, until wave 7 adds `app.ws`; this is the dispatcher mapping that FR-HTTP-008 AC-7 relies on. [D-395; T06; FR-ROUTE-015]

After `app.route(Method.any().except(Method.DELETE), "/t", h)`, `DELETE /t` through the in-memory harness is answered `405` with `Allow` = `GET, HEAD, POST, PUT, PATCH, OPTIONS` (the router's `Method` declaration order, FR-ROUTE-010 AC-1) and `Content-Length: 0` in wave 3. [D-395] [T02]

records.title: Interim handler failure and unfinished-response handling

acceptanceCriteria.text: A handler that throws `RuntimeException` before writing anything is answered `500` with an empty body through the harness. [wave decision: Interim failure handling]

A handler that throws a checked `IOException` after setting status `201` but before commit is answered `500` with an empty body. [wave decision: Interim failure handling] Decision: the status and headers the handler set are dropped and the `500` carries only `Content-Length: 0`; the exception is not rethrown to the adapter. [SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-3-3 SDS-AC-8]

A handler that throws after commit while the response is `STREAMING` (the only committed-but-incomplete state a wave 3 handler can reach) leaves the response `ABORTED` and the in-memory adapter reports the exchange closed abnormally instead of a `500`; a handler that throws after the response is `COMPLETED` (for example after `res.send("x")`) leaves it `COMPLETED`, because abort is a no-op there, with the sent bytes unchanged and no `500`. [D-097; D-099; wave decision: abort() after completion; wave decision: Interim failure handling]

A handler that sets `status(202)` and `header("X-A", "1")` and returns without a body write or `end()` yields `202` with `X-A: 1` and an empty body, and the response is `COMPLETED`. [wave decision: Interim failure handling] Decision: when the handler returns with the response `NEW` the dispatcher calls `end()`, and with it `STREAMING` it runs the pending stream copy on the same adapter thread. [SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-3-3 SDS-AC-10]

records.title: Internal RestApp implementation with deferred router build and freeze

acceptanceCriteria.text: The implementation is a public class in a package documented as internal and not part of the API contract, it implements `RestApp`, and it holds the router and the dispatcher. [wave decision: Working app in wave 3; D-393] Decision: the implementation is public class `DefaultRestApp` in package `com.snoworca.naruserve.internal`, whose package javadoc states it is not API. [SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-3-3 SDS-AC-14]
A registration with an invalid pattern (one that `RoutePattern.parse` rejects) throws at the registration call itself, before any freeze. [wave decision: Working app in wave 3; D-047; D-048]

`app.get("/a/b", h)` followed by `app.routerPolicy(RouterPolicy.builder().mergeSlashes(true).build())` makes `GET /a//b` reach `h` after the harness freeze, showing the policy applies to registrations made before it. [wave decision: Working app in wave 3; FR-ROUTE-006]

The `Router` is constructed only at the freeze, and a duplicate of D-044 surfaces as the freeze's `RoutingConfigException`, not at the second registration call. [wave decision: Working app in wave 3; D-044] Decision: the freeze propagates the `RoutingConfigException` unchanged and leaves the app unfrozen, so `dispatcher()` keeps throwing `IllegalStateException`. [SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-3-3 SDS-AC-12]

After the harness freeze, `app.get(...)`, `app.route(Method, path, h)`, `app.route(MethodSet, path, h)` and `app.routerPolicy(...)` each throw `IllegalStateException`, and `RouteBuilder` registration methods (`get`, `put`, ...) throw `IllegalStateException` too, including on a builder obtained from `app.route(path)` before the freeze. [wave decision: Settings after the freeze] Decision: the internal WebSocket-route hook also throws `IllegalStateException` after the freeze, and a refused call records nothing. [SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-3-3 SDS-AC-13]
No public static method or constructor in package `com.snoworca.naruserve` returns a `RestApp` in wave 3. [wave decision: Working app in wave 3; D-111]

The internal implementation (not the public `RestApp` interface) offers an internal WebSocket-route registration hook that records a WebSocket registration and passes it to `Router.addWebSocket` at the freeze; the test-fixtures harness uses it to register a WebSocket-only route, and wave 3 dispatches no handshake to that route (a matching upgrade request gets the same `426` as a plain `GET`) until wave 7 adds `app.ws`. [D-395; T06; wave decision: Working app in wave 3]

records.title: Request path, raw path and path parameter accessors

acceptanceCriteria.text: For `GET /files/a%20b?x=1` matched by `/files/:name`, `req.path()` returns `/files/a b`. [D-073] Decision: `req.path()` percent-decodes the raw path once as UTF-8, keeps `+` as `+`, and applies no `mergeSlashes`, trailing-slash or case policy. [SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-3-4 SDS-AC-1] Under `mergeSlashes(true)`, `GET /a//b` matched by `/a/b` gives `req.path()` = `/a//b` (the policy affects only route matching, not the decoded path). [wave 3 implementation decision]
For the same request `req.rawPath()` returns `/files/a%20b`, without `?x=1`. [D-074; wave decision: Remaining markers]
For the same request `req.param("name")` returns `a b`. [D-075]

`req.param("missing")` for a name not in the matched pattern throws an exception instead of returning `null`. [D-075] Decision: the exception is `IllegalArgumentException` and its message contains the name. [SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-3-4 SDS-AC-2]

records.title: Query accessors with form-urlencoded decoding and malformed-query 400

acceptanceCriteria.text: For `?a=1&a=2&b=3`, `req.query("a")` returns `1`, `req.queries("a")` returns `[1, 2]`, `req.query("c")` returns `null` and `req.queries("c")` returns an empty list. [D-076; T07]

For `?q=a+b%20c&%ED%95%9C=%EA%B8%80`, `req.query("q")` returns `a b c` and `req.query("한")` returns `글`. [D-077; T07] Decision: a pair without `=` has the empty string as its value, empty names are kept, and names and values decode `+` as space. [SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-3-4 SDS-AC-3]

A query `?x=%zz`, a query `?x=%E0%A4` (truncated UTF-8) and a query `?x=%C3%28` (invalid UTF-8) are each answered `400` and the matched handler is not called. [D-078; T07; wave decision: Interim failure handling] Decision: a malformed `%XX` or bytes that are not valid UTF-8 (decoder `CodingErrorAction.REPORT`) make the query parse throw `IllegalArgumentException`, which the dispatcher answers `400` with `Content-Length: 0` before the handler runs. [SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-3-4 SDS-AC-4]

records.title: Response body writers send, html, stream and end

acceptanceCriteria.text: `res.send("hé")` writes the UTF-8 bytes `68 C3 A9` with `Content-Type: text/plain; charset=UTF-8`, and after `res.header("Content-Type", "text/csv")` it keeps `text/csv`. [D-091] Decision: a body writer adds its default `Content-Type` only when no `Content-Type` header is set, compared case-insensitively. [SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-3-5 SDS-AC-2]

`res.html("

é

")` writes UTF-8 bytes with `Content-Type: text/html; charset=UTF-8`. [D-092]

`res.send(new byte[]{0, (byte) 0xFF, 10})` writes exactly those three bytes with `Content-Type: application/octet-stream` when none was set, and keeps an explicitly set `Content-Type`. [D-093; wave decision: Remaining markers]

`res.stream(in, "application/pdf")` with a 1 MiB input writes all bytes in order with `Content-Type: application/pdf`, and a counting input stream shows that every `read(byte[], int, int)` call requests fewer bytes than the 1 MiB input. [D-094] Decision: the copy reads with an 8192-byte buffer and writes each chunk to the exchange output stream in order. [SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-3-5 SDS-AC-3]

`res.stream(...)` closes the input stream exactly once after a successful copy, after a read failure, and after `res.abort(...)` during the transfer, including when the handler already returned; the caller does not close it. [D-094; wave decision: stream() closing] Decision: the single close is guarded by a compare-and-set. [SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-3-5 SDS-AC-4]

`res.end()` completes the response with the status and headers set so far and no body. [D-095] Decision: on a non-bodyless response `end()` commits with `Content-Length: 0`. [SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-3-5 SDS-AC-6]

`res.stream(InputStream, contentType)` does not block until the copy ends: it commits the response and returns, the copy to the end of the stream runs after the handler returns, and the response is `STREAMING` until the copy ends; a test whose handler returns right after `res.stream(...)` observes the call return before the input is read to its end. [D-094; D-103; wave decision: stream() closing] Decision: `stream` sets `Content-Type` to the argument, commits with unknown length, enters `STREAMING` and returns; the dispatcher runs the copy on the adapter thread after the handler returns. [SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-3-5 SDS-AC-5]

records.title: Response commit flag, abort and header CR/LF rejection

acceptanceCriteria.text: `res.isCommitted()` is `false` before any body write and `true` after `res.send("x")` handed the status and headers to the in-memory adapter. [D-096] Decision: `abort` before any commit leaves `isCommitted()` `false`, sets `ABORTED` and aborts the exchange without writing a status. [SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-3-5 SDS-AC-8]
`res.abort(new IOException("x"))` during a `stream(...)` transfer makes the in-memory adapter report the connection closed abnormally and leaves the response state `ABORTED`. [D-097]

`res.abort(...)` on a response that is already `COMPLETED` or `ABORTED` does nothing: no exception, the state is unchanged and the adapter sees no further close. [wave decision: abort() after completion]

`res.header("X\r\nY", "1")`, `res.header("X", "a\nb")` and `res.header("X", "a\rb")` each throw an exception and add no header. [D-098] Decision: the exception is `IllegalArgumentException`, the header list stays unchanged, and the response-state check runs first. [SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-3-5 SDS-AC-7] Besides CR and LF, `res.header` also throws `IllegalArgumentException` for a name that is not an RFC 9110 token (empty, or a char outside tchar) and for a value holding any control character other than HTAB (such as NUL or DEL) or any char above U+00FF. [wave 3 implementation decision]

records.title: Response state machine with single commit

acceptanceCriteria.text: A response starts in `NEW`, is `COMMITTED` once status and headers are handed to the adapter, and reaches `COMPLETED` after `send`; the adapter receives the status line and headers exactly once. [D-099]

`res.status(500)` or `res.header("X", "1")` after `res.send("a")` committed the response throws an exception and the sent status and headers stay unchanged. [D-100] Decision: the exception is `IllegalStateException` naming the current state, thrown in `COMMITTED`, `STREAMING`, `COMPLETED` or `ABORTED`, and nothing changes. [SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-3-5 SDS-AC-10]
A second body call (`send`, `html`, `stream` or `end`) after a body was sent throws an exception and writes no further bytes. [D-101]

After `res.stream(...)` returns, the response is `STREAMING` until the copy ends, then `COMPLETED`, or `ABORTED` on abort; a read failure of the input stream during the copy, including after the handler returned, ends the response `ABORTED` with the input stream closed (FR-HTTP-014 AC-5). [D-103; D-097; wave decision: stream() closing] Decision: a read failure during the copy sets `ABORTED`, calls `exchange.abort()` and closes the input, without rethrowing to the adapter. [SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-3-5 SDS-AC-11]

While the response is `STREAMING` (committed but not completed), `res.status(500)` and `res.header("X", "1")` each throw an exception and the status and headers the adapter received stay unchanged. [D-100; D-099]

records.title: Request body ownership with BodyState and BodyAlreadyConsumedException

acceptanceCriteria.text: `BodyAlreadyConsumedException` is a public class in `com.snoworca.naruserve` extending `RuntimeException`. [D-086; wave decision: Body ownership]

`BodyState` is an internal class whose state is `UNREAD` initially, `PARSING` while a reader holds the body, and `CONSUMED` after a completed read or `CLOSED` after the body was closed; a unit test drives each transition. [D-085] Decision: `close` moves to `CLOSED` from any state, and a later `begin` or shared parse throws `BodyAlreadyConsumedException`. [SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-3-4 SDS-AC-11]

[D-086] Decision: `begin` in any state other than `UNREAD` throws `BodyAlreadyConsumedException` naming the current state. [SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-3-4 SDS-AC-9]

A unit test acquiring the shared form/multipart parse through `BodyState` repeatedly gets the same parse result each time without a second read of the stream and without `BodyAlreadyConsumedException`. [D-087] Decision: the shared parse after `begin`, or `begin` after the shared parse, throws `BodyAlreadyConsumedException`; a parser failure leaves `CONSUMED` with no cached result and later calls throw `BodyAlreadyConsumedException`. [SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-3-4 SDS-AC-10]
A reflection test finds no public body-reading method on `Request` at the wave 3 merge (wave 5 adds the body readers). [wave decision: Body ownership]

records.title: Dispatcher pipeline and pre-request checks before route lookup (wave 4)

acceptanceCriteria.text: Through the harness, a `GET /users/7` request with `app.get("/users/:id", h)` registered reaches `h` once with a `Request` and a `Response`, and the status, headers and body `h` wrote come back through the in-memory adapter. [D-394; D-397]

With a recording handler registered through `app.route(Method.any(), "/", h)` and `app.route(Method.any(), "/:x", h)`, `OPTIONS *` is answered `204` before path validation (so `*` is not rejected with `400`), and a validator rejection happens before the router lookup: `GET /%2e%2e` and `GET /a%2Fb` (both rejected by the `PathValidator`) are answered `400`, no lookup exception escapes, and `h` registered on the matching pattern `/:x` records no call. [wave decision: Order before lookup; D-442; D-052] Decision: the dispatcher checks in this order: `OPTIONS` with raw path `*` gives `204`, any raw path not starting with `/` gives `400`, a `PathValidator` rejection gives `400`, then the router lookup runs. This order applies to requests that passed the lifecycle gate; the unrecognised-method-token `501` comes after the validator check and before a `Request` is built.

A raw path that the wave 2 `PathValidator` rejects is answered `400` with the standard error body of FR-APP-006 (`code` `BAD_REQUEST`, `Content-Type: application/json; charset=UTF-8`) without a router lookup, and the validator sees the raw form with a single decoding: `/%2e%2e` and `/a%2Fb` are answered `400`, while `/%252e%252e` reaches a `/:x` route with `req.param("x")` = `%2e%2e`. [wave-3 carried: path validator before lookup; D-052; wave-4 carried: standard error body; D-134]

An unrecognised method token is answered `501`, a raw path not starting with `/` `400`, a validator rejection `400` and `OPTIONS *` `204`, each before a `Request` is built, so no middleware, handler or `onError` sees them; a recording global middleware, a recording `onError` and a recording handler registered through `app.route(Method.any(), "/", h)` and `app.route(Method.any(), "/:x", h)` record that they were never called. [wave-3 residual: pre-request rejections; D-422; wave decision: Pre-request rejections]
In every handler and middleware call `req.method()` returns a non-null `Method` and `req.path()` a non-null decoded path. [wave-3 residual: pre-request rejections; I-014]
The HTTP-level assertions of T01, T02, T03, T05 and T06 run as tests through the in-memory adapter and the harness in `./gradlew build`. [D-397]

records.requirement: The system shall provide a dispatcher that takes each exchange from an `HttpAdapter` that passed the lifecycle gate of FR-APP-009 and FR-APP-013, checks the asterisk-form `OPTIONS *` first, then rejects a raw path not starting with `/` with `400`, then rejects a raw path refused by the wave 2 path validator with `400`, and only then calls the router lookup and either runs the middleware pipeline and the matched `RouteHandler` with a `Request` and a `Response` or writes the automatic response, where the pre-request rejections are answered before any `Request` is built, so no middleware, handler or `onError` sees them, and the two `400` rejections carry the standard error body.

records.title: Automatic responses for router lookup results with the standard error body (wave 4)

acceptanceCriteria.text: Through the harness, a request whose path matches no route is answered `404` with the standard error body of FR-APP-006 (`code` `NOT_FOUND`). [D-395; wave-4 carried: standard error body; D-134]

With only `POST /p` registered, `GET /p` is answered `405` with `Allow` listing `POST, OPTIONS`, and with `GET /r` registered `DELETE /r` is answered `405` with `Allow` including the automatic `HEAD` and `OPTIONS`, both with the standard error body (`code` `METHOD_NOT_ALLOWED`). [D-395; T02; D-134] Decision: the `Allow` value joins the allowed methods (or `Method.any()` for `OPTIONS *`) with `, ` in `MethodSet` iteration (`Method` declaration) order.

With `GET /r` and `POST /r` registered and no `OPTIONS` route, `OPTIONS /r` is answered `204` with `Allow` = `GET, HEAD, POST, OPTIONS`, no body and no `Content-Length` header. [D-395; T05; wave decision: Automatic response bodies]

`TRACE /x` with `TRACE` disabled and `CONNECT /` with `CONNECT` disabled are each answered `501` with the standard error body (`code` `NOT_IMPLEMENTED`) after the global middleware ran, while a request with an unrecognised method token (FR-ROUTE-013) is answered `501` with the standard error body before any `Request` is built, as FR-HTTP-021 AC-4 states. [D-395; wave decision: 426 and 501; wave decision: Pre-request rejections; D-422] Decision: the dispatcher tells the two cases apart by whether the method token parses to a `Method` value.

With a WebSocket-only route registered through the internal hook of FR-HTTP-008 AC-7, a plain `GET` to that path is answered `426` with headers `Upgrade: websocket` and `Connection: Upgrade` and the standard error body (`code` `UPGRADE_REQUIRED`), asserted through the in-memory adapter. [D-395; T06; wave decision: 426 over TinyHttpd; wave decision: 426 and 501] Decision: the upgrade flag passed to the lookup is `Router.isWebSocketUpgrade(token, Connection, Upgrade)` with each header's values joined by `, `.

With the same WebSocket-only hook route, a `GET` carrying `Upgrade: websocket` and `Connection: Upgrade` (for which the router returns a `MATCHED` result with route kind `WEBSOCKET`) is answered with the same `426`, both headers and the standard error body, and no handshake is attempted, until wave 7 adds `app.ws`. [D-395; T06; FR-ROUTE-015]

After `app.route(Method.any().except(Method.DELETE), "/t", h)`, `DELETE /t` through the in-memory harness is answered `405` with `Allow` = `GET, HEAD, POST, PUT, PATCH, OPTIONS` (the router's `Method` declaration order, FR-ROUTE-010 AC-1) and the standard error body. [D-395; T02]

[D-442; D-052]

A raw path `abc` and a raw path `*` with method `GET` are each answered `400` with the standard error body of FR-APP-006 (`code` `BAD_REQUEST`) without route lookup, and the access log records one line for each. [D-442; wave-4 carried: standard error body; wave decision: Pre-request rejections]

records.title: Handler failure and unfinished-response handling through the wave 4 error path

acceptanceCriteria.text: A handler that throws `RuntimeException` before writing anything is answered `500` with the standard error body of FR-APP-006 (`code` `INTERNAL_ERROR`) through the harness when no `onError` is registered. [D-127; D-132; wave-4 carried: interim failure handling replaced]

A handler that throws a checked `IOException` after setting status `201` and header `X-A: 1` but before commit is answered `500` with the standard error body; the status and headers the handler set are dropped and the exception is not rethrown to the adapter. [D-127; D-132; D-134]

A handler that throws after commit while the response is `STREAMING` (the only committed-but-incomplete state a handler can reach before wave 5) leaves the response `ABORTED` and the in-memory adapter reports the exchange closed abnormally instead of a `500`; a handler that throws after the response is `COMPLETED` (for example after `res.send("x")`) leaves it `COMPLETED`, because abort is a no-op there, with the sent bytes unchanged and no `500`. [D-097; D-099; D-131; wave decision: abort() after completion]

A handler that sets `status(202)` and `header("X-A", "1")` and returns without a body write or `end()`, and a middleware that returns without responding or calling `next.run()`, each yield the status and headers set so far (`202` with `X-A: 1`, and `200` for the middleware case) with an empty body, the response is `COMPLETED`, and the app logger received one `warn` naming the method and path. [D-126] Decision: the finishing behaviour is a `warn` through the app logger followed by `end()`; with the response `STREAMING` the dispatcher runs the pending stream copy on the same adapter thread and logs no warning.

records.requirement: The system shall answer an exception thrown by a handler or middleware through the error path of FR-APP-005, which gives the standard `500` error body while the response is not committed and no `onError` responded, abort the response when the exception is thrown after commit or while streaming, and, when the chain returns with the response not started and no `next.run()`, log a developer warning through the app logger and finish the response with the status and headers set so far and an empty body without waiting for a timeout.

records.title: Query accessors with form-urlencoded decoding and malformed-query 400 through the error path (wave 4)

acceptanceCriteria.text: For `?a=1&a=2&b=3`, `req.query("a")` returns `1`, `req.queries("a")` returns `[1, 2]`, `req.query("c")` returns `null` and `req.queries("c")` returns an empty list. [D-076; T07]

For `?q=a+b%20c&%ED%95%9C=%EA%B8%80`, `req.query("q")` returns `a b c` and `req.query("한")` returns `글`. [D-077; T07] Decision: a pair without `=` has the empty string as its value, empty names are kept, and names and values decode `+` as space.

A query `?x=%zz`, a query `?x=%E0%A4` (truncated UTF-8) and a query `?x=%C3%28` (invalid UTF-8) are each answered `400` with the standard error body of FR-APP-006 (`code` `BAD_REQUEST`) and the matched handler is not called. [D-078; T07; wave-4 carried: malformed query reaches middleware and onError] Decision: a malformed `%XX` or bytes that are not valid UTF-8 (decoder `CodingErrorAction.REPORT`) make the query parse raise `HttpException` with status `400`; the dispatcher parses the query after the middleware ran and before the handler, so global and prefix middleware run, a middleware that reads `req.query(...)` receives that exception, and it reaches `onError` through the error path of FR-APP-005. The query is parsed after the route middleware ran and before the handler; a request without a matched route gets the fallback answer (`404`, `405`, ...) and its query is parsed only if a middleware reads it.

records.requirement: The system shall decode the raw query string as UTF-8 `application/x-www-form-urlencoded` text with `+` read as a space, make `req.query(name)` return the first value or `null` and `req.queries(name)` every value in request order or an empty list, and answer a query with malformed percent-encoding or invalid UTF-8 with `400` and the standard error body through the error path, after the middleware ran and before the handler runs.

records.title: Middleware and Next interfaces and the middleware registration methods

acceptanceCriteria.text: Reflection finds `Middleware` annotated `@FunctionalInterface` with the single abstract method `void handle(Request, Response, Next) throws Exception`, and `Next` with exactly the abstract methods `void run()` and `void error(Throwable)`; a Java lambda `(req, res, next) -> next.run()` compiles as a `Middleware`. [D-115; D-116]

`RestApp` declares `use(Middleware)`, `use(String, Middleware)`, the seven overloads `get|post|put|patch|delete|head|options(String, Middleware, RouteHandler)` and `route(Method, String, Middleware, RouteHandler)` and `route(MethodSet, String, Middleware, RouteHandler)`, each returning `RestApp`, and every wave 3 `RestApp` method keeps its signature. The wave 3 surface test of IR-HTTP-005 AC-5 (a statement about the wave 3 merge) is re-pointed to the wave 4 method set: the wave 3 methods plus those of IR-APP-002, IR-APP-003, IR-APP-005, IR-APP-006 and IR-APP-007, with `create()` and `builder()` as the only static methods. [D-119; I-014; D-137] Decision: the route-middleware overloads return `RestApp` like the plain registration methods.

`RouteBuilder` declares `use(Middleware)` returning `RouteBuilder`; middleware added through it applies as route middleware to every method the same builder registers after the `use` call, in `use` call order, so `app.route("/a").use(m1).use(m2).get(h)` runs `m1`, `m2`, then `h` for `GET /a`. [D-137; D-120] Decision: `RouteBuilder.use(middleware)` is adopted and is the way to attach several route middleware; no varargs or multi-middleware overload is added to `RestApp`.

`use(null)`, `use("/api", null)`, `use(null, mw)` and every route-middleware overload with a `null` middleware or handler throw `NullPointerException`, and `use(prefix, mw)` with a prefix that does not start with `/` throws `IllegalArgumentException`. [D-118; D-119]

No public type of `NaruServe-api` declares a method that resumes a middleware chain from another thread or returns a future, and `Next` has no method other than `run()` and `error(Throwable)`. [D-128]

A Kotlin test in `NaruServe-api` compiles and runs `app.use { req, res, next -> next.run() }`, `app.use("/api") { req, res, next -> next.run() }` and `app.get("/x", mw) { req, res -> res.send("x") }` without a DSL. [D-115; C-03]
