records.title: Lifecycle API: AppState, onStart/onStop, listen, ServerHandle and shutdown

acceptanceCriteria.text: `AppState.values()` is exactly `NEW, STARTING, RUNNING, STOPPING, FAILED, TERMINATED` in that order, and `app.state()` of a newly built app is `NEW`. [D-152]

Reflection finds `LifecycleCallback` annotated `@FunctionalInterface` with the single abstract method `void handle(ApplicationContext) throws Exception`, and `RestApp.onStart(LifecycleCallback)` and `RestApp.onStop(LifecycleCallback)` returning `RestApp`; `onStart(null)` and `onStop(null)` throw `NullPointerException`. [D-137] Decision: `onStart` and `onStop` share the callback interface `LifecycleCallback`, which may throw `Exception`.

`ServerHandle` declares exactly `int port()`, `String address()` and `AppState state()`; after `listen(0)` succeeded `port()` returns the adapter's `boundPort()`, `address()` returns `127.0.0.1` and `state()` returns the app's current state, so it reads `TERMINATED` after shutdown. [D-155] Decision: the accessors are `port()`, `address()` and `state()`, and `listen` binds to `127.0.0.1`.

`listen(port)` with a port outside `0..65535` throws `IllegalArgumentException` and leaves the state `NEW`; `shutdown(timeout, unit)` with a negative timeout throws `IllegalArgumentException` and with a `null` unit `NullPointerException`. [D-153; D-161]

`AppStartException` extends `RuntimeException`; it is the type `listen()` throws for a checked start-failure cause (as its cause) and for a start ended by a pending stop. [D-159; D-426] Decision: the unchecked wrapper type is `AppStartException`.
A Kotlin test compiles and runs `app.onStart { ctx -> ctx.attribute("k", 1) }`, `val h = app.listen(0)`, `h.port()`, `app.state()` and `app.shutdown(1, TimeUnit.SECONDS)`. [D-152; D-155; C-03]

records.title: Logger SPI, LogLevel, the console logger and app.logger

acceptanceCriteria.text: Reflection finds on `Logger` exactly the six abstract methods `trace(String)`, `debug(String)`, `info(String)`, `warn(String)`, `error(String)` and `error(String, Throwable)`, and `LogLevel.values()` is `TRACE, DEBUG, INFO, WARN, ERROR`. [D-168; wave decision: Logger shutdown]

`new ConsoleLogger()` writes `info`, `warn` and `error` records and drops `trace` and `debug`; `new ConsoleLogger(LogLevel.TRACE)` writes all five levels. Each record is one line `<timestamp> <LEVEL> <message>` where the timestamp is formatted with `SimpleDateFormat("yyyy-MM-dd'T'HH:mm:ss.SSSZ")` (offset like `+0900`; no `java.time`, no `X` pattern, both absent from Android API 21), checked by a test under two time zones, `TRACE`/`DEBUG`/`INFO` go to `System.out` and `WARN`/`ERROR` to `System.err`, and `error(m, t)` writes the stack trace of `t` after the line. [D-169; D-181] Decision: the console logger defaults to threshold `INFO` and uses this line format.
`ConsoleLogger#close()` and `flush()` flush both streams and leave `System.out` and `System.err` open, so a later `System.out.println` still prints. [wave decision: Logger shutdown]

`app.logger(l)` makes `app.logger()` return `l`, `app.logger()` before any call returns the builder's logger (the console logger by default), and `app.logger(null)` throws `NullPointerException`; `logger(l)` is under the `NEW`-state guard of FR-APP-002 while `logger()` is readable in every state. [D-170; D-114]
`ConsoleLogger` is in `NaruServe-api` and references no SLF4J or `android.*` type. [D-169; D-178]

records.requirement: The system shall declare in `com.snoworca.naruserve` the interface `Logger` with exactly `trace(String)`, `debug(String)`, `info(String)`, `warn(String)`, `error(String)` and `error(String, Throwable)`, the enum `LogLevel` (`TRACE`, `DEBUG`, `INFO`, `WARN`, `ERROR`), and the public console logger `ConsoleLogger implements Logger, Flushable, AutoCloseable` that is the default app logger of `RestApp.builder()`, and shall add to `RestApp` the methods `Logger logger()` and `RestApp logger(Logger logger)`.
records.rationale: Covers D-168, D-169 (the console logger and its default for the explicit entry point; the `create()` half is wave 5), D-170 and the D-181 decision on the console line format. The wave decision on logger shutdown keeps the six `Logger` methods.

records.title: Access log configuration API

acceptanceCriteria.text: `app.accessLog(options -> options.enabled(true).level(LogLevel.DEBUG).includeRequestId(false).includeDuration(false).includeBytes(false).exclude("/health"))` compiles and returns the app, and each option method returns the same `AccessLogOptions` instance. [D-172]

Without any `accessLog` call the access log is enabled at level `INFO` with request id, duration and bytes included and no excluded path; two `accessLog` calls apply both configurers to the same options in call order. [D-181; D-172] Decision: these are the defaults, and `accessLog` calls accumulate.
`accessLog(null)`, `level(null)` and `exclude(null)` throw `NullPointerException`, and `accessLog` is under the `NEW`-state guard of FR-APP-002. [D-172; D-114]
`Configurer` is annotated `@FunctionalInterface`, and a Kotlin test compiles `app.accessLog { it.exclude("/health") }`. [D-172; C-03]

records.requirement: The system shall declare the generic `@FunctionalInterface` `Configurer<T>` with `void configure(T target)` and the configuration type `AccessLogOptions` with `enabled(boolean)`, `level(LogLevel)`, `includeRequestId(boolean)`, `includeDuration(boolean)`, `includeBytes(boolean)` and `exclude(String path)`, each returning the options, and add `RestApp accessLog(Configurer<AccessLogOptions> configurer)` with the defaults enabled, level `INFO`, request id, duration and bytes included, and no excluded path.
records.rationale: Covers D-172 and the D-181 decision on the option defaults. `Configurer<T>` avoids `java.util.function` in the public API (Android API 21) and is the shape later `multipart(config -> ...)` and `staticFiles(..., options -> ...)` reuse.

records.title: Request and Response public surface of wave 3

acceptanceCriteria.text: `Request` is a public interface in `com.snoworca.naruserve` declaring `method()`, `path()`, `rawPath()`, `param(name)`, `query(name)`, `queries(name)`, `header(name)`, `headers(name)`, `remoteAddress()`, `isSecure()`, `lastEventId()`, `attribute(key, value)` and `attribute(key, type)`, with `method()` returning `Method`. [D-071] Decision: the write overload `attribute(String, @Nullable Object)` returns `void` and the read overload is generic `<T> @Nullable T attribute(String, Class<T>)`, so a literal `null` second argument resolves to the read overload. [SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-3-1 SDS-AC-1]

`Response` is a public interface in `com.snoworca.naruserve` declaring `status(code)`, `header(name, value)`, `send(String)`, `send(byte[])`, `html(String)`, `stream(InputStream, contentType)`, `end()`, `isCommitted()` and `abort(error)`. [D-071] Decision: `status` and `header` return the receiver; `send`, `html`, `stream`, `end` and `abort` return `void`. [SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-3-1 SDS-AC-2]

At the wave 3 merge, a reflection test finds no method named `body`, `form`, `file`, `files`, `parts`, `json`, `download`, `cache`, `sse`, `cookie`, `getCookies`, `addCookie`, `service` or `application` on `Request` or `Response`, even where the parameter and return types of such a method exist in wave 3; the later waves of D-392 add them. D-072 is met by the wave 1 convention: package `com.snoworca.naruserve` is annotated JSpecify `@NullMarked` (non-null by default, which counts as `@NonNull`) and every nullable reference-type parameter or return value of `Request` and `Response` carries `@Nullable`; a reflection test checks the package annotation and the `@Nullable` positions that `docs/api/request.md` and `docs/api/response.md` list as nullable (such as the returns of `query`, `header` and `attribute(key, type)`). [D-072] Decision: exactly these positions carry `@Nullable`: the returns of `query`, `header`, `lastEventId` and `attribute(key, type)`, and the parameters `value` of `attribute(key, value)` and `error` of `abort(error)`. [SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-3-1 SDS-AC-3]

A Kotlin source test compiles and runs calls to the wave 3 `Request` and `Response` methods, assigning `req.query("q")` to `String?` and `req.path()` to `String` without platform types. [D-072] Decision: the Kotlin test routes a request through the test-fixtures `TestApp` harness and calls every wave 3 `Request` and `Response` method from a Kotlin lambda. [SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-3-1 SDS-AC-4]

records.title: HttpAdapter SPI exchange data contract

acceptanceCriteria.text: The SPI exposes, per request, the request line as the method token, the raw request-target path, the raw query string (or its absence) and the HTTP version, plus the header names and values in received order, a body `InputStream`, the remote address and the secure flag. [D-105] Decision: the headers are exposed as a `List<Map.Entry<String, String>>` in received order with duplicates kept, not as a `Map`. [SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-3-2 SDS-AC-1]

The SPI accepts from the core a status code, response headers and a body `OutputStream`, and the core writes status and headers before the first body byte. [D-105] Decision: status, headers and the content length (`-1` when unknown) pass in one `commit` call that returns the body `OutputStream`, and a second start of the response throws `IllegalStateException`. [SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-3-2 SDS-AC-2] The exchange outlives `ExchangeHandler#handle` until the core calls `finish` or `abort`, and the adapter may force-close it only at its stop deadline; `abort()` is idempotent and thread-safe (it may run on any thread, also while another thread is in `commit`, a body write or `finish`, which then fail with an `IOException`). The headers passed to `commit` are sent as given: they already carry `Content-Length` when the core knows it (a `HEAD` response carries the length the `GET` body would have had) and the adapter never adds, removes or changes `Content-Length`; `contentLength` is the number of body bytes the core will write, `0` for a bodyless response (`204`, `304`, `HEAD`) or `-1` when unknown, which the adapter frames itself (chunked, or close on HTTP/1.0) and is the only case where it may add a framing header. Header names and values are ISO-8859-1: the core guarantees every char is at most U+00FF and never CR or LF, so the adapter writes each char as one byte. [wave 3 implementation decision]

The raw request-target path and the raw query string travel through the SPI as separate undecoded fields: an exchange with target `/a%20b?x=%41` reaches the core with raw path `/a%20b` and raw query `x=%41`, and the core alone yields `req.path()` = `/a b` and `req.query("x")` = `A`. [D-399; wave decision: Adapter halves] Decision: the raw query is `null` when the target has no `?`. [SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-3-2 SDS-AC-3]

records.title: HttpAdapter SPI extension points and bind/stop lifecycle

acceptanceCriteria.text: Through the file-transfer extension point the core hands the adapter a `java.io.File` with an offset and a length, and the adapter writes exactly those bytes of the file as the response body; an in-memory test hands over a file with a non-zero offset and a length shorter than the rest of the file and reads back exactly that byte range from the client body. [D-106]

Through the protocol-upgrade extension point the core hands the adapter an upgrade callback with a `101` response, and the adapter invokes that callback with the exchange's raw input and output streams after writing the `101` response; an in-memory test observes that the callback ran with the exchange's streams (or that the in-memory adapter recorded the hand-over). [D-106]

The event-stream point hands the adapter a core-owned drain loop that keeps writing after the handler returned until the core reports the stream ended, and the adapter chooses the thread that runs it; in wave 3 (before `res.sse` exists) an in-memory test supplies a drain loop through the SPI type, runs it on an adapter-chosen thread after the handler returned and sees it end only when the end is reported. [D-106] Decision: `eventStream` returns to the caller at once, and the in-memory adapter runs the drain on its own worker thread, completing the client response when the drain returns. [SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-3-2 SDS-AC-4]

The three extension points are SPI types in `NaruServe-api`, usable by an adapter without any NaruServe class outside `NaruServe-api`, so waves 6, 7 and 8 add adapter classes against them without changing the SPI. [D-106]

The SPI declares a bind to an address and port that returns only after binding completed, and a separate call through which the core reads the actual bound port; with the in-memory adapter, a bind with port `0` reports a positive bound port that the core reads back through the SPI and that stays the same on every read until stop, and a bind with a positive port reports that port. [D-107] Decision: for a bind with port `0` the in-memory adapter assigns a positive port from a counter starting at `49152`. [SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-3-2 SDS-AC-5]

The SPI declares a blocking stop that stops accepting, waits for in-flight exchanges until a deadline passed by the core and then force-closes the remaining connections, and a separate final release that waits at most a fixed margin for the adapter's threads to end; the in-memory adapter implements both and a test shows an in-flight exchange still running at the deadline is force-closed. [D-107] Decision: an exchange in flight at the deadline is aborted so its client response reports `abnormallyClosed`, and the in-memory adapter's release shuts its worker pool waiting at most 1 second. [SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-3-2 SDS-AC-6]

records.title: Immutable MethodSet combinators

acceptanceCriteria.text: For `MethodSet s = Method.get()`, calling `s.post()` returns a set containing `GET` and `POST`, and `s` still contains only `GET` afterwards; the same holds for every combinator and for `except`. [D-033] [SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-2-1 SDS-AC-4] Every combinator, `with` and `except` returns a different `MethodSet` instance unless the members are unchanged, and leaves the receiver's members unchanged.

`Method.get().post().except(Method.POST)` contains exactly `GET`, and `except` of a method that is not a member returns a set equal to the receiver. [D-035]
`MethodSet` has no public constructor or mutator, its fields are final, and any iterator or collection it exposes is unmodifiable (`remove` throws `UnsupportedOperationException`). [D-033]

records.title: Lookup result contract and precedence

acceptanceCriteria.text: The result type exposes exactly six kinds and each lookup returns exactly one; the matched kind carries the handler, the path parameters, the actual method (the request method for a direct match, `GET` under automatic `HEAD` and for a WebSocket match; it does not decide the wave 3 `req.method()` value, D-398), the route kind and the automatic-`HEAD` flag, and the method-mismatch and automatic-OPTIONS kinds carry an `Allow` `MethodSet`. [D-390] [SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-2-3 SDS-AC-1] A field a kind does not carry reads as null (handler, method, route kind, allow) and params reads as an empty map.

An unrecognised method token yields unsupported method even when no pattern matches the path, and a recognised method on a path no pattern matches yields no match. [wave decision: lookup result order]
On a matched path a route of the request method wins over automatic OPTIONS and automatic `HEAD`, which win over WebSocket-only, which wins over method mismatch. [wave decision: lookup result order]

The lookup takes the raw, undecoded path as received in the request target, so a lookup of `GET /files/%252e` against `GET /files/:name` yields `name` = `%2e`; the path is checked with the path validator before any result is chosen, so a rejected path such as `/a%zz` fails with `IllegalArgumentException` for every method token, and "whatever the path" elsewhere in this scope means whatever accepted path. [D-051; loop W residual: validator does not decode] [SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-2-3 SDS-AC-2] The `IllegalArgumentException` names the path and is thrown before the method token is read.

The upgrade flag is ignored unless the method token is `GET`; registering a route after the freeze fails with `IllegalStateException`, a lookup before a successful freeze fails with `IllegalStateException`, and the routing configuration error is an exception type of its own (name decided under C-07), distinct from `IllegalStateException` and `IllegalArgumentException`. [wave decision: route kind; D-058]

records.title: TinyHttpd composite build through a Gradle property

acceptanceCriteria.text: `docs/api/request.md` states that `rawPath()` returns the raw, undecoded path without the query string (available through `req.query(...)`), gives its Express counterpart as `req.path` before decoding (not `req.originalUrl`), and has no (미확정) marker on the `rawPath()` row. [D-109; wave decision: Remaining markers]

`docs/api/request.md` states that `req.attribute(name, type)` throws `ClassCastException` for a stored value of another type, without a marker, and that a value is removed by storing a typed `null` variable because a literal `null` resolves to the read overload. [D-109; wave decision: Remaining markers; wave decision: Null attribute values]

`docs/api/response.md` states that `send(byte[])` without a `Content-Type` uses `application/octet-stream` and that `stream(InputStream, contentType)` takes ownership and closes the stream on success, failure or abort, with an example that does not use try-with-resources, and the marker line on these two points is gone. [D-109; wave decision: stream() closing; wave decision: Remaining markers]

`docs/api/routing.md` documents `app.routerPolicy(RouterPolicy)` with `RouterPolicy.builder()` (`mergeSlashes`, `ignoreTrailingSlash`, `caseInsensitive`, `enableTrace`, `enableConnect`) as allowed only while the app is in `NEW` (before `listen()`), like every setting in `app.md` (in wave 3 the internal implementation rejects a call after the harness freeze with `IllegalStateException`, FR-HTTP-008), replaces the sentence of section '라우팅 규칙 (wave 2 결정)' saying the policy setting API name is not decided with a pointer to `app.routerPolicy(RouterPolicy)` so that no sentence calls that name undecided, and states that `req.method()` returns `HEAD` during automatic `HEAD`; its marker set is checked by OPS-ROUTE-002 AC-3. [D-398; wave decision: Remaining markers; wave decision: req.method() during automatic HEAD; wave-3 residual: marker test of wave 2]
`docs/api/app.md` lists `routerPolicy(RouterPolicy)` among the `RestApp` methods with a Java and a Kotlin example and adds no (미확정) marker for it. [D-398; wave decision: Remaining markers]

`docs/api/defaults.md` names `app.routerPolicy(...)` with `enableTrace`/`enableConnect` as the explicit `TRACE`/`CONNECT` policy, and that row has no (미확정) marker. [D-398; wave decision: Remaining markers]

`docs/api/express-migration.md` no longer maps `req.originalUrl` to `req.rawPath()`: the `rawPath()` row names `req.path` before decoding as its Express counterpart without a marker, and a kept `req.originalUrl` row points to `req.rawPath()` plus the query string read through `req.query(...)` or states that it has no direct counterpart, without a marker; the `express.raw()`/`express.text()` marker is replaced with the statement that v1 has no raw or text body reader, and the raw/text bullet is removed from the undecided list (section 'Express에 있지만 아직 정해지지 않은 기능'), so the file states once, without contradiction, that v1 has no raw or text body reader. [D-109; wave decision: Remaining markers; wave decision: Body ownership] Decision: the kept `req.originalUrl` row points to `req.rawPath()` plus the query read through `req.query(...)`. [SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-3-6 SDS-AC-5]

Markers other than those this requirement removes stay, including `file` disposition and `redirect` in `response.md`, proxy trust, `parts()` and `jsonTree()`/`jsonMap()` in `request.md`, `RouteBuilder.use` in `routing.md`, and the markers of `express-migration.md` owned by other issues. `docs/api/request.md` states that `req.attribute(name, type)` throws `ClassCastException` for a stored value of another type, without a marker, and that a value is removed by storing a typed `null` variable because a literal `null` resolves to the read overload. [D-109; wave decision: Remaining markers; wave decision: Null attribute values]

`docs/api/response.md` states that `send(byte[])` without a `Content-Type` uses `application/octet-stream` and that `stream(InputStream, contentType)` takes ownership and closes the stream on success, failure or abort, with an example that does not use try-with-resources, and the marker line on these two points is gone. [D-109; wave decision: stream() closing; wave decision: Remaining markers]

`docs/api/routing.md` documents `app.routerPolicy(RouterPolicy)` with `RouterPolicy.builder()` (`mergeSlashes`, `ignoreTrailingSlash`, `caseInsensitive`, `enableTrace`, `enableConnect`) as allowed only while the app is in `NEW` (before `listen()`), like every setting in `app.md` (a call outside `NEW` is rejected with `IllegalStateException` by the state guard of FR-APP-002), replaces the sentence of section '라우팅 규칙 (wave 2 결정)' saying the policy setting API name is not decided with a pointer to `app.routerPolicy(RouterPolicy)` so that no sentence calls that name undecided, and states that `req.method()` returns `HEAD` during automatic `HEAD`; its marker set is checked by OPS-ROUTE-003 AC-3. [D-398; wave decision: Remaining markers; wave decision: req.method() during automatic HEAD; wave-3 residual: marker test of wave 2]
`docs/api/app.md` lists `routerPolicy(RouterPolicy)` among the `RestApp` methods with a Java and a Kotlin example and adds no (미확정) marker for it. [D-398; wave decision: Remaining markers]

`docs/api/defaults.md` names `app.routerPolicy(...)` with `enableTrace`/`enableConnect` as the explicit `TRACE`/`CONNECT` policy, and that row has no (미확정) marker. [D-398; wave decision: Remaining markers]

`docs/api/express-migration.md` no longer maps `req.originalUrl` to `req.rawPath()`: the `rawPath()` row names `req.path` before decoding as its Express counterpart without a marker, and a kept `req.originalUrl` row points to `req.rawPath()` plus the query string read through `req.query(...)` or states that it has no direct counterpart, without a marker; the `express.raw()`/`express.text()` marker is replaced with the statement that v1 has no raw or text body reader, and the raw/text bullet is removed from the undecided list (section 'Express에 있지만 아직 정해지지 않은 기능'), so the file states once, without contradiction, that v1 has no raw or text body reader. [D-109; wave decision: Remaining markers; wave decision: Body ownership] Decision: the kept `req.originalUrl` row points to `req.rawPath()` plus the query read through `req.query(...)`. [SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-3-6 SDS-AC-5]

Markers other than those this requirement and OPS-APP-001 remove stay, including `file` disposition and `redirect` in `response.md`, proxy trust, `parts()` and `jsonTree()`/`jsonMap()` in `request.md`, and the markers of `express-migration.md` owned by issues other than #4, #5, #6 and #7; `routing.md` keeps no marker once wave 4 decides `RouteBuilder.use`, and `HttpDocsTest` is re-pointed to this requirement. records.title: Access log never records secrets and escapes control characters

acceptanceCriteria.text: A request `POST /login?token=qzv&password=pwz` with `Authorization: Bearer s3cr3t`, `Cookie: sid=c00k1e` and body `password=pwq2` whose handler answers `token-xyz` produces a line that contains none of `qzv`, `pwz`, `s3cr3t`, `c00k1e`, `pwq2`, `token-xyz` or `?`. [D-175; T39]

A raw path containing `%0d%0a` is logged with the raw percent-encoded form, and an unrecognised method token or path containing a CR, LF, TAB, `0x01`, `0x7F` or `0x85` character is logged with `\r`, `\n`, `\t` and `\u0001`, `\u007f`, `\u0085`, and `\` as `\\`, so every access log record is one line. [D-176; T39] Decision: control characters U+0000–U+001F, U+007F and U+0080–U+009F are escaped this way.
The access log line holds no header value at all. [D-175]

records.requirement: The system shall keep `Authorization` and `Cookie` header values, passwords, tokens, request and response bodies, multipart content and the query string out of the access log line, and escape CR, LF and every other control character in each logged value.
records.rationale: Covers D-175 and D-176 (T39).
